correctness.rationale: Exact Bellman recursion from common additive valuations and max envy = absolute load difference. Backward suffix induction proves monotonicity and exceptional state bounds for every finite word on {1,2}; these certify optimal greedy moves from all reachable imbalances 0,1,2. Explicit four-item costs and a monotone two-stage continuation prove the sharp failure and minimal length. CHECK.py passed 8191 binary words, 2047 suffix-invariant words, 820 three-item integer words, and 18 four-item witnesses. No finite search is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic exact dynamic programming covers these numerical instances algorithmically, but it does not prove that the myopic path is optimal. Prefix-EF1/MMS existence guarantees do not imply minimum total cumulative envy. No stronger searched theorem was found that implies the new claim.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating full text proves greedy minimum summed prefix envy for identical {0,1} valuations (Section 4, Proposition 1 and Appendix 0.B.1), not for strictly positive unequal {1,2}. Its generic dynamic program is not an optimality theorem for a myopic rule. The {1,2} proof needs new suffix Bellman inequalities; a per-stage bound fails already at (1,1,2). The 2025 personalized two-value and the 2026 mixed-manna works use MMS/EF criteria rather than minimum summed prefix envy. No directly equivalent statement appeared in the literature records examined. Similarity searches cannot certify worldwide novelty; scheduling/discrepancy aliases remain a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent signed-prefix discrepancy theorem in combinatorics, online balancing, or two-machine scheduling is possible.
The full texts of two secondary comparator papers were not material-read; the accessible stated results do not imply the candidate theorem.
No independent publication-priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The source introduced cumulative maximum envy as a temporal fairness objective and gave generic complexity and dynamic-programming results. A zero-lookahead irrevocable algorithm that is globally optimal for all fixed-order positive {a,2a} instances materially simplifies deployment, even though stagewise minima cannot all be attained. The exact integer-value and four-item frontiers explain a natural boundary; this is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor merely a renaming of known {0,1} results.
